must_fix: (criterion 1/10) Two program artifacts flatly disagree about XOM's correct SEC CIK, and the deliverable only shows one side. outputs/b1_report.md line 359 ('Lineage fix') states as a resolved fact that 'SEC now lists XOM under ExxonMobil Holdings Corp (CIK 2115436, reorganisation 2026-08)' and that the pipeline was fixed accordingly (D3 lineage / D1 multi-CIK links, live rank recomputed to 99). The wave-3 dossier (outputs/f59_summary.json XOM entry) and FINAL_REPORT.md §11 instead say 'the correct SEC CIK... is 0000034088' and call the discrepancy 'unresolved.' I independently queried SEC EDGAR for both: CIK 2115436 = ExxonMobil Holdings Corp, one 10-Q on file (filed 2026-08-03, accession 0000034088-26-000093 -- note the accession prefix is CIK 34088, i.e. it was filed as a co-registrant on the operating company's own filing); CIK 34088 = Exxon Mobil Corp (formerly Exxon Corp), most recent 10-K filed 2026-02-18. Both CIKs are real and both filed in 2026; the dossier's claim that one is simply 'correct' and the b1_report's claim that the pipeline fix is settled cannot both be the final word without reconciling why the two disagree. Zero current portfolio impact (XOM is WATCH, not held), but it shows cross-artifact facts are not checked against each other before publication. Fix: add a short note in FINAL_REPORT §11 (or b1_report.md) explaining the actual co-registrant relationship between the two CIKs and which one the pipeline vs. the dossier each queried and why, rather than letting one call it fixed and the other call it unresolved.

(criterion 4) DA9/DA10 (42 facts across MA, AXP, MSCI, CAH, COR, VEEV) achieved a strong 97.6% strict-pass rate (1 FAIL: COR's initial FY2026 revenue-guidance figure and its Q1 'reaffirmed' characterization were both wrong, correctly identified and quoted from the releases; 1 MINOR: MSCI's kill-criterion-2 'a year ago' label was actually two quarters, not four), both properly corrected in dated dossier Correction sections I verified. But this is the same failure pattern flagged in Loop 5 (DA7: entity/segment conflation) recurring in a different form (guidance-checkpoint mislabelling) -- a first-draft dossier error caught only by the adversarial DA pass, not by the authoring analyst. The Loop-5 must-fix proposing a cheap mechanical pre-check (grep for entity/temporal qualifiers next to a claimed figure) was not implemented before wave-3; recommend building it before any wave-4 diligence rather than continuing to rely solely on after-the-fact DA correction.

(minor, criterion 6) The persisted portfolio weights (outputs/lead_portfolio_build.json 'weights') sum to 0.999999, not exactly 1.0 -- I summed all 20 values myself. This is a display-precision artifact (each weight stored to 6 decimals independently) worth under $1 on a $100,000 sleeve and does not affect any cap check (all six checks in the build's own 'checks' array, which I independently recomputed to the same 6 decimals, still pass), but the checks array's own printed value of '1.0' for this test is not the literal stored-weight sum. Store the pre-rounding weights alongside the display-rounded ones, or increase precision, so the persisted numbers used by any downstream script exactly match what the check claims.

(carried, not a new defect) Verification gate (code/lead_verify_gate.py) correctly reads OPEN, for exactly one reason: outputs/c1_consistency.json still names content_sha256 ee5f7079... (an earlier, pre-wave-3 build) while the frozen build this audit covers is 31e96bf8... -- expected, since C1 is deliberately run last, after this audit's fixes. I confirmed no holding is missing an independent DA-series fact-check and no FAIL is left uncorrected. Close this only by re-running C1 against the final post-fix build before packaging the next release, as already planned.
